title: Finite no-regret bound for normalized convex-compact games
statement:
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ and $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ satisfy the convex-compact minimax hypotheses, and suppose the payoff is normalized so that $0 \le f(x,y) \le 1$ for all $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$. Then for every nonempty finite subset $u \subseteq X$,
\[
  \inf_{x \in X} \sup_{y \in Y} f(x,y)
    \;\le\;
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in u} f(x,y);
\]
that is, the game's upper value is bounded above by the lower value of the game in which the row player is restricted to the finite sample $u$ while the column player still ranges over all of $Y$.
hypotheses_covered: convex-compact minimax hypotheses on X, Y, f
payoff normalized: 0 ≤ f(x,y) ≤ 1 for all x ∈ X, y ∈ Y
conclusion holds for every nonempty finite subset u ⊆ X
replaced:
Under the convex-compact minimax hypotheses and $0 \le f \le 1$,
$\texttt{OnlineLearning.Theorem71FiniteNoRegretBound}$ holds.  This removes the artificial
$\mathrm{Fin}\,M$ indexing from
$\texttt{OnlineLearning.theorem71\_finiteIndexedNoRegretBound\_normalized}$; the singleton
case is handled separately since the finite minimax theorem requires at least two row
actions.
